title: Integration Boost measurement is outsourced to the Core Council Risk Advisor and published at a named third-party API
content:
Every Integration Boost Instance names the same two things. The Data Submission Format (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.2.1.1.5 and siblings): "The Data Submission Responsible Actor calculates the net deposits based on on-chain events and makes the data available through an API endpoint located at https://info-sky.blockanalitica.com/api/v1/incentivized-pools/." And the Responsible Actor (…1.1.6): "the Core Council Risk Advisor."

The separation is the point. The party that pays the boost is Skybase; the party that measures the deposits determining the boost is a Core-level advisor. Neither the Agent nor the partner controls the number, which removes the obvious incentive problem on both sides — Skybase cannot understate deposits to reduce its bill, and the partner cannot inflate them.

That independence is bought with a specific, unusual dependency: a live HTTPS endpoint on a named external analytics provider is written into a governance document as the canonical delivery channel. If that endpoint changes, moves, or goes down, an Artifact-level parameter is stale — and the boost calculation has no documented fallback in these Instances.

It is also worth noting what is *not* specified. "Net deposits based on on-chain events" describes the quantity but not the algorithm — no contract addresses, no netting window, no treatment of edge cases. Compared with the Distribution Reward primitive, where CoW Swap's Tracking Methodology is spelled out in detail, Integration Boost delegates methodological discretion to the Risk Advisor rather than fixing it in text.
description: The Data Submission Responsible Actor computes net deposits from on-chain events and serves them at a Block Analitica URL written into the Artifact — so Skybase does not measure its own spending.
